Container.Name: nova-prime-chummer
Container.Overview: Nova Prime Chummer: a character generator and career tracker for Shadowrun Anarchy 2.0 and Shadowrun 6. It's a browser app you run on your own network: create runners with Ganger, Runner or Prime Runner packages, build Shadow Amps, track a career ledger, and print a character sheet. Runners are saved as XML files in the Characters folder, a folder per account (deleted ones go to its .trash). Put overlay XML (house rules, extra gear, private descriptions) in the Custom data folder and list it in custom/index.xml. The app ships no book content, not even the core rules: on first start, import the core rulebook PDF on the Books page, or upload a data pack (a small file of just the core tables) from another server. Upload your other PDFs the same way; they are kept in the Library folder and imported into Custom data/imported. Imports can miss descriptions or details: any amp, item, spell or rule can be edited, and new entries added under your own house-rule source; edits are kept in Custom data/edits and survive re-imports. Settings → Backup downloads everything (runners, edits, imported data, uploaded PDFs, AI settings; API keys only if you tick it) as one zip, and Restore from backup puts it back after saving a safety copy to Library/.backups. Sign-in: on first start the container log shows a one-time setup code that creates the first admin; the admin adds everyone else (admin, editor or player). Behind a reverse proxy, set Trusted proxy.

Config.Name: Characters
Config.Description: Saved runners: a folder per account, one XML file per runner

Config.Name: Custom data
Config.Description: House-rule and extra-content XML overlays (list them in index.xml), imported book data and your catalog edits (edits/)

Config.Name: Library
Config.Description: Your uploaded PDFs, their converted text, import reports, AI settings (keys) and automatic safety backups (.backups). Never served over the web.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User id the server runs as; the data folders are handed to it on start. 99 is Unraid's nobody.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group id the server runs as. 100 is Unraid's users.

Config.Name: Trusted proxy
Config.Description: The IP address of your reverse proxy, e.g. 192.168.1.10 (several: comma-separated IPs or CIDRs). Only requests from these addresses may set X-Forwarded-For/-Proto/-Host, which decide the client address (sign-in limits, logs), https (secure cookie) and the public address. List every hop that adds X-Forwarded-For: with Cloudflare in front of NGINX Proxy Manager, add Cloudflare's published ranges too (or have NPM restore the real IP). Don't list a whole subnet or the Docker gateway while the port is published. Leave empty when there is no proxy.

Config.Name: Public address
Config.Description: Optional: the one address people use, e.g. https://chummer.example.com (no path). When set, the sign-in checks and the Authelia redirect URI use it instead of the request's Host, and the app is only usable at that address. Leave empty to use the Host (and X-Forwarded-Host from a trusted proxy).
